pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Illinois does not use one single statewide journeyman electrician exam for every candidate. Journeyman electrician licensing and credentialing are commonly handled by local jurisdictions, and requirements can vary depending on the city, county, village, or local authority involved. Candidates should follow the requirements for the jurisdiction where they plan to work or where their employer requires the credential. A commonly used journeyman-level electrical exam format is the ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam. That exam includes 80 multiple-choice questions, allows 4 hours of testing time, and is open book. The exam content areas include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam content places strong emphasis on wiring methods and materials, branch circuits and conductors, equipment and devices, services and service equipment, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions. These areas reflect the kind of code-based knowledge a journeyman-level electrician is expected to apply in the field. Some Illinois jurisdictions may use different local exams, local electrical codes, local amendments, separate application rules, or different testing providers. Chicago, for example, has its own electrical licensing structure and local code requirements. Because Illinois licensing is local, the exact exam name, code edition, passing score, reference list, fee, and application process can vary by jurisdiction. This Ultimate Combo is focused on 2026 NEC-based journeyman electrician exam preparation.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: It is useful for candidates who need a structured way to study journeyman-level electrical topics, practice calculations, improve NEC navigation, and work through exam-style questions before taking a local or recognized journeyman electrician exam.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates taking that exam may use approved references during the examination, subject to the exam provider’s rules. Because Illinois journeyman electrician testing can vary by local jurisdiction, candidates should follow the exam-room rules for the specific exam they are approved to take. Open book testing still requires serious preparation. The National Electrical Code is a detailed technical reference, and candidates who do not know how it is organized can lose time searching through the wrong articles or tables. A strong candidate should know how to identify the subject of a question, choose the correct NEC area, locate the applicable rule, and apply it accurately. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is designed to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: During study, candidates can use the tabbed NEC to become familiar with definitions, general requirements, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, communications systems, tables, and calculation-related provisions. Open book does not mean every answer will be easy to find. Some questions may require trade knowledge, electrical theory, calculations, or practical judgment. Others may require candidates to compare code sections, understand exceptions, use table notes, or apply a rule to a specific installation condition. Timed practice is one of the best ways to prepare for this type of exam. Candidates should also understand that exam-room reference rules may limit tabs, handwritten notes, loose papers, printed materials, or reference editions. The NEC included in this package is for study and code-navigation practice. Whether a candidate may use a specific book in the exam room depends on the approved reference rules issued for that exam.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Illinois journeyman electrician licensing steps depend on the local authority that issues or recognizes the credential. A candidate may need to apply through a city building department, county office, village licensing division, local electrical commission, or other municipal authority. Because Illinois does not issue one statewide journeyman electrician license, candidates should identify the local jurisdiction first. A typical Illinois journeyman electrician path may include completing electrical apprenticeship or supervised work experience, gathering employer verification, collecting training documentation, submitting a local application, paying required local fees, scheduling an approved journeyman-level exam, passing the required examination, and completing the remaining local licensing or registration steps. Some jurisdictions may require a certain number of years of field experience, apprenticeship completion, proof of employment under a licensed electrical contractor, continuing education, identification documents, or a local sponsor.

Requirements can vary, so candidates should organize documents based on the local application instructions. Application Service is included with this Ultimate Combo. It does not guarantee exam eligibility, local approval, license issuance, employment qualification, or a passing score. Candidates should keep clear records of work history, apprenticeship hours, classroom training, employer information, project types, dates of employment, and any previous electrical credentials. Good documentation can help with local applications and may also support future licensing goals.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Illinois does not have a single statewide journeyman electrician license issued to individual electricians. Electrical licensing is primarily handled through local governments. Cities, counties, and villages may set their own requirements for journeyman electricians, electrical contractors, registrations, exams, renewals, and local work authorization. Because of this local structure, an Illinois journeyman electrician candidate should confirm the requirements for the exact jurisdiction where the credential is needed. A city may require a local examination, while another municipality may recognize a license from another Illinois jurisdiction. Some areas may focus on contractor registration rather than individual journeyman licensing, and some employers may require a journeyman-level credential as part of their hiring or jobsite requirements.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Common preparation areas for Illinois journeyman electrician candidates include National Electrical Code knowledge, electrical theory, services, feeders, branch circuits, conductors, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, motors, control devices, equipment, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and electrical calculations. Candidates should also understand the difference between a journeyman electrician credential and electrical contracting authority. A journeyman credential generally supports trade-level recognition and employment, while electrical contracting may require a separate contractor license, registration, insurance, bonding, or local business authorization. This Ultimate Combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code. Code-cycle alignment matters because definitions, article language, table notes, wiring methods, and installation requirements can change between NEC editions. pieces.t: Yes. This Super Combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs for study and code navigation practice.

pieces.h: Q: Why is the Electrician Calculations Study Guide included?
pieces.t: Electrical calculations are important for master-level preparation. The calculations guide helps candidates practice formulas, load calculations, conductor sizing, motor calculations, transformer concepts, and other math-based electrical topics.

pieces.h: Q: Are the flash cards useful for Illinois electrical exam preparation?
pieces.t: Yes. Flash cards are useful for quick review of formulas, definitions, electrical theory, safety concepts, NEC topics, and trade knowledge. They work well alongside longer study sessions and timed practice.

pieces.h: Q: Do I need to check my local Illinois licensing authority?
pieces.t: Yes. Because Illinois electrical licensing is local, candidates should confirm the exact license title, application steps, exam provider, reference rules, code edition, fees, insurance requirements, and renewal rules for the jurisdiction where they plan to work.

pieces.h: Q: What books are included in this combo?
pieces.t: This package includes the 2026 Illinois Master Electrician Study Guide, the 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide, and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: Is there one statewide Illinois master electrician license?
pieces.t: Illinois electrical licensing is generally handled by local jurisdictions rather than one single statewide master electrician license. Candidates should check the requirements for the city, county, or municipality where they plan to apply.

pieces.h: Q: Who should use this study combo?
pieces.t: This combo is intended for electricians preparing for Illinois master electrician exam content, NEC-based questions, and electrical calculation problems. It is especially useful for candidates who want both code study and calculation practice in one package.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package help with electrical calculations?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates practice electrical math, formulas, table use, and calculation-based exam topics.

pieces.h: Q: Can I use the NEC paperback for studying?
pieces.t: Yes. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback is included so candidates can study directly from the code book, review articles and tables, and improve NEC navigation skills.

pieces.h: Q: Are Illinois master electrician exams open book?
pieces.t: Exam rules can vary by local jurisdiction. This combo supports code-book study and NEC navigation, and candidates should follow the official testing instructions from the authority administering their exam.

pieces.h: Q: Does this combo guarantee that I will pass the exam?
pieces.t: No. No study product can guarantee a passing score or licensing approval. This combo provides organized study support, code review, calculation practice, and preparation structure based on the 2026 NEC.
